newsitem.title: LEBANON: Rostropovich to reopen Lebanon's Baalbek Festival.
newsitem.headline: Rostropovich to reopen Lebanon's Baalbek Festival.

text.p: The Baalbek Festival, once Lebanon's leading cultural event, will resume in July with a performance by cellist Mstislav Rostropovich after a 23-year gap, the festival committee announced on Thursday.

The Baalbek Festival, held annually from 1956 to 1974 with performers like Rostropovich, ballet stars Margot Fonteyn and Rudolf Nureyev, conductor Herbert von Karajan and pianist Sviatoslav Richter, was halted by Lebanon's 1975-90 civil war.

Rostropovich and the Orchestre Philharmonique de Radio France will reopen it on July 30 with a performance on the steps of the Roman Temple of Bacchus inside the Baalbek acropolis, committee president May Arida told Reuters.
The committee has been trying to restart the festival, which is held amid spectacular Roman ruins, since the war ended but has received government support only this year.
This year's festival will feature two other spectacles apart from Rostropovich which have not yet been decided, Arida said.

However, she doubted that Western-style ballet would be included because the militant Shi'ite Moslem group Hizbollah (Party of God) which made Baalbek its stronghold during the civil war would not approve.
